title: Who Has Believ'd Thy Word
description: Who Has Believ'd Thy Word in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 141, headed “The humiliation and exaltation of Christ, Isa. 53. 1-5 10 11 12”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Who has be-liev'd thy word, Or thy sal-va-tion known? Re-veal thine arm, al-might-y Lord, And glo-ri-fy thy Son.

lines: But 'twas their grief upon him lay,
The God of justice pleas'd to bruise
"Shall quit their prisons and their graves;
"Who saw the follies men had done,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
